post.caption: This square diamond has its corners cut. Joseph Asscher of Amsterdam developed the Asscher cut in 1902, and its square outline has cropped corners that read as an octagon. The original design has 58 facets, and a high crown and deep pavilion create a hall of mirrors effect. It became popular in the 1920s, during the Art Deco era, and production of the original stopped around World War II. Asscher's firm also cut the Cullinan diamond in Amsterdam in 1908, and in 1980 Queen Juliana granted the firm the title Royal. Around 2001 the family introduced the Royal Asscher cut with 74 facets. An Asscher cut is square, while an emerald cut is rectangular.
